## Interviews

### ZDF (German public television)
**2026 · October 21** · Interview with correspondent Salim Sadat

A taped interview for ZDF's long-form story on the 2026 midterm elections and how much influence the Latino vote carries. The segment has not aired yet.

### WHYY (Philadelphia NPR), *Studio 2*
**2026 · October 5** · ["Will Latino Voters Swing Back to Democrats?"](https://whyy.org/episodes/will-latino-voters-swing-back-to-democrats/)

A live segment on WHYY's public affairs hour, alongside Mike Madrid, on the range of issues and beliefs that move Latino voters ahead of the midterms. Audio and video are on the episode page.

### CNHI News
**2026 · September** · ["Latinos Viewed as Key Swing Vote in Midterms"](https://www.register-herald.com/news/state_region/latinos-viewed-as-key-swing-vote-in-midterms/article_ab82b3c1-36db-52af-ac9f-7f7355b1c56e.html), by Christian M. Wade

A national story on Latino voters' role in the midterms, with control of Congress hinging on thin margins. It was syndicated across CNHI's newspapers; the link goes to the version in *The Register-Herald*.

### Deutsche Welle
**2025 · February 15** · ["¿Se arrepienten latinos en EE. UU. de haber votado a Trump?"](https://laopinion.com/2025/02/15/se-arrepienten-latinos-en-ee-uu-de-haber-votado-a-trump/) (in Spanish; republished by *La Opinión*)

A DW feature on viral memes claiming Latino Trump voters regret their vote. I argue the memes overlook that a Latino voter is, by definition, not undocumented, and that mocking these voters amounts to blaming them when Democrats have not done enough to reach them since at least 2016.

### *The Latino Vote* podcast, with Chuck Rocha and Mike Madrid
**2025 · February 7** · ["Kitchen Table Issues: A Look at Latino Independent Voters"](https://thelatinovote.buzzsprout.com/1952477/episodes/16583000-kitchen-table-issues-a-look-at-latino-independent-voters-with-dr-derek-wakefield)

The show's first guest episode of 2025. We talk about my research on how Latino voters, and independents especially, put economic issues ahead of the identity and immigration appeals that campaigns usually lead with.

## Coverage

### *The Latin Times*
**2026 · October** · ["Allentown's Latino Vote Could Flip the House. Here's What's at Stake"](https://www.latintimes.com/allentowns-latino-vote-could-flip-house-heres-whats-stake-599767)

A look at Allentown's Latino electorate in a pivotal House race. It draws on my finding that shifts in Latino partisanship track economic perceptions far more closely than immigration or identity appeals.

## Press Release Coverage

Local coverage of Bucknell's press release on my research: Latino voters respond to economic conditions more than any other major group of American voters, which could make inflation, jobs, and household finances decisive in the midterms.
